chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

"Any woman who is divorced, and her husband dies before her waiting period (iddah) expires, she inherits him, and then she observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died for her. And if she dies during her waiting period, he inherits her. And if she is killed, he inherits from her blood money (diyah). And if he is killed, she inherits from his blood money, provided that one of them did not kill the other."

key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rights of a divorced woman if her ex-husband dies before her waiting period ends?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the legal status of a *mutallaqa* (divorced woman) whose ex-husband dies during her waiting period, confirming she inherits as a widow and completes her *iddah* accordingly. It further extends inheritance rights to blood money (*diyah*) in cases of homicide, provided the killer is not the spouse, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of reciprocal financial liability. This ruling is foundational in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for distinguishing between full marital inheritance and the specific rights of the divorced waiting period.
